capabilities: Transcribe handwritten ink into Markdown, LaTeX, Mermaid or SVG at the cursor
Annotate with a separate AI pen to give the model instructions without them counting as content
Flag suspicious transcription with a warning instead of silently fixing it
Connect to Claude or an OpenAI-compatible vision service with a user-provided API key
Open the pad from the editor context menu or the Handwrite command
extras: Each conversion sends an image of the ink plus surrounding note text to the provider; cost is roughly one to three US cents per page with Claude Opus 5.5. Requires Obsidian 1.11.4 or later, is built for iPad and Apple Pencil (a mouse works on desktop), and is MIT licensed with development notes hosted elsewhere. The manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian only accepts typed input, so there is no built-in way to handwrite on a tablet and get the result into a note as Markdown.

relations.evidence: In its settings, pick Claude or an OpenAI-compatible service.

requires.name: Claude or an OpenAI-compatible vision service

summary: Handwriting pad that turns tablet ink into Markdown at the cursor—text, LaTeX, Mermaid or SVG—via Claude or another vision model.
